record.title: Trump Signs DHS Funding Bill Ending the Shutdown
record.description_short: Trump signed DHS funding legislation that ended the shutdown while excluding ICE and CBP Border Patrol from its appropriations.
record.description_medium: On April 30, 2026, Donald Trump signed a DHS funding measure that ended the shutdown. It funded most DHS agencies through fiscal year 2026, excluding ICE and CBP Border Patrol from its appropriations; employees of those agencies were then being paid under a prior reconciliation law. The bill provided $48 billion for covered agencies.
record.description_long:
On April 30, 2026, President Donald Trump signed a bill that funded most Department of Homeland Security operations and ended the agency’s shutdown. The measure provided Fiscal Year 2026 funding for covered DHS agencies, totaling $48 billion, while excluding Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Customs and Border Protection’s Border Patrol; employees of those agencies were being paid through the previous year’s reconciliation law. It identified funded components including the Federal Emergency Management Agency, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services, Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, Transportation Security Administration, Coast Guard, and Secret Service.

The measure also included oversight provisions addressing the administration’s immigration-related policies. It directed DHS to develop a uniform policy making federal law-enforcement personnel clearly identifiable, increased funding for DHS’s Office of Inspector General by $37 million, a 20 percent increase, and provided funding for the Office for Civil Rights and Civil Liberties and the Office of the Citizenship and Immigration Services Ombudsman. The congressional release said the action would restart federal employees’ paychecks and allow services, including FEMA disaster response and Coast Guard operations, to resume.
